verses.text: Ben-Hadad king of Syria gathered his whole army. Thirty-two kings were with him, with their horses and chariots. He went up, surrounded Samaria, and attacked it.
He sent messengers into the city to Ahab king of Israel to say, "This is what Ben-Hadad says:
'Your silver and gold are mine, and your wives and your best children are mine too.'"
The king of Israel answered, "Just as you say, my master the king. I am yours, and everything I have is yours."
The messengers came back and said, "This is what Ben-Hadad says: 'I sent you a message saying, "Give me your silver, your gold, your wives, and your children."
But about this time tomorrow I will send my officials to you. They will search your palace and the houses of your officials. They will take away everything you value.'"

Then the king of Israel called together all the leaders of the land and said, "See how this man is looking for trouble! When he sent for my wives, my children, my silver, and my gold, I did not refuse him."
All the leaders and all the people said to him, "Do not listen to him, and do not agree to it."

So Ahab told Ben-Hadad's messengers, "Tell my master the king, 'I will do everything you asked your servant the first time, but I cannot do this.'" The messengers left and took the answer back to Ben-Hadad.
Then Ben-Hadad sent another message to Ahab: "May the gods punish me, and even more, if there is enough dust left in Samaria for each of my soldiers to get a handful!"
The king of Israel answered, "Tell him, 'A man putting on his armour should not boast like a man taking it off after the battle.'"
Ben-Hadad heard this message while he and the kings were drinking in their tents. He said to his officials, "Get ready to attack!" So they got ready to attack the city.
Then a prophet came to Ahab king of Israel and said, "This is what the LORD says: 'Do you see this huge army? I am going to hand it over to you today. Then you will know that I am the LORD.'"

Ahab asked, "Who will do it?" The prophet said, "This is what the LORD says: 'The young officers of the district governors will do it.'" Ahab asked, "Who will start the battle?" The prophet answered, "You will."
So Ahab called up the young officers of the district governors, two hundred and thirty-two men. Then he called up the rest of the Israelites, seven thousand in all.
They marched out at noon. Ben-Hadad and the thirty-two kings helping him were in their tents, getting drunk.
The young officers of the district governors went out first. Ben-Hadad's scouts reported to him, "Men are coming out of Samaria."
He said, "Whether they have come out to make peace or to fight, take them alive."
The young officers of the district governors marched out of the city, with the army behind them.
Each one killed the enemy soldier he fought. The Syrians ran away, and Israel chased them. But Ben-Hadad king of Syria escaped on a horse with some of his horsemen.
The king of Israel went out and attacked the horses and chariots, and he defeated the Syrians with heavy losses.
Afterward, the prophet came to the king of Israel and said, "Go and make your army stronger, and think about what you must do, because next spring the king of Syria will attack you again."

Meanwhile, the officials of the king of Syria told him, "Their gods are gods of the hills. That is why they were too strong for us. But if we fight them on the flat land, we will surely be stronger than they are.
Do this: remove all the kings from their commands and put army officers in their places.

Build an army like the one you lost, horse for horse and chariot for chariot. Then we will fight Israel on the flat land, and we will surely be stronger than they are." He agreed with them and did it.
The next spring Ben-Hadad gathered the Syrians and went up to Aphek to fight against Israel.
The Israelites were also gathered and given supplies, and they marched out to meet them. The Israelites camped facing them like two little flocks of goats, while the Syrians covered the countryside.

A man of God came to the king of Israel and said, "This is what the LORD says: 'The Syrians think the LORD is a god of the hills and not a god of the valleys. So I will hand this whole huge army over to you, and you will know that I am the LORD.'"
For seven days the two armies camped facing each other. On the seventh day the battle began. The Israelites killed one hundred thousand Syrian foot soldiers in one day.
The rest ran away into the city of Aphek, and the wall fell on twenty-seven thousand of them. Ben-Hadad also ran into the city and hid in an inner room.

His officials said to him, "Look, we have heard that the kings of Israel are merciful. Let us put on sackcloth, tie ropes around our heads, and go out to the king of Israel. Maybe he will spare your life."

So they put on sackcloth and tied ropes around their heads. They went to the king of Israel and said, "Your servant Ben-Hadad says, 'Please let me live.'" Ahab answered, "Is he still alive? He is my brother."

The men were watching for a good sign, and they quickly caught his word. "Yes, your brother Ben-Hadad!" they said. Ahab said, "Go and bring him." When Ben-Hadad came out, Ahab had him climb up into his chariot.

Ben-Hadad said to him, "I will give back the towns my father took from your father. You may set up your own market streets in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria." Ahab said, "With this agreement I will set you free." So he made a treaty with him and let him go.
By the LORD's command, one of the prophets' group said to another, "Please hit me!" But the man refused to hit him.
So the prophet said, "Because you did not obey the LORD, as soon as you leave me a lion will kill you." And as soon as the man left, a lion found him and killed him.
Then the prophet found another man and said, "Please hit me." So the man hit him and wounded him.
Then the prophet went and waited by the road for the king. He disguised himself by pulling his headband down over his eyes.

As the king passed by, the prophet called out to him, "Your servant went into the middle of the battle, and a man came over to me with a prisoner. He said, 'Guard this man. If he goes missing, you will pay for his life with your life, or else pay about thirty-four kilograms of silver.'
But while your servant was busy here and there, the man disappeared." The king of Israel said to him, "That is your sentence. You have said it yourself."
Then the prophet quickly pulled the headband away from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized him as one of the prophets.

The prophet said to the king, "This is what the LORD says: 'You have set free the man I had marked for destruction. So your life will take the place of his life, and your people the place of his people.'"
The king of Israel went home to Samaria, sulking and angry.
